Assessment Calendar Doc

Guidance on Active Proctoring

Active proctoring means staying alert, mobile, and engaged throughout the entire testing period — not seated at a desk. Consistent, attentive proctoring protects testing integrity, supports students who need redirection or reassurance, and ensures a fair, standardized testing environment for every student.

  • Circulate continuously through the room; avoid remaining in one spot or sitting for extended periods.
  • Monitor for students who finish early, appear stuck, or show signs of distress, and respond according to test protocol.
  • Keep cell phones and personal devices put away, and ensure students do the same.
  • Watch for and prevent any unauthorized collaboration, talking, or use of prohibited materials.
  • Know accommodations for students with IEPs/504 plans in advance and apply them correctly.
  • Follow all timing procedures exactly, including start times, breaks, and stop times.

School Trips

School-wide guidance, permission forms, and procedures for planning and taking student trips.

Field Trip Guidance & Forms Chancellor Regulations on Field Trips

Field Trip Policies & Procedures

All field trips, except those arranged by the administration, must receive the principal's approval at least four weeks before the planned trip. Each classroom teacher must submit a separate Field Trip Request Form for their class. Required field trip forms are available in the main office. The Field Trip Request Form used to secure transportation must be completed and submitted before the trip is confirmed.

*Please review Field Trip Guidance for full details on planning and procedures.

  • Every 10 children must have a chaperone.
  • Collect funds in advance from students for any needed admission fees, tolls, and/or parking. A parent's inability to pay is not a valid reason for not taking a student on a trip — please consider this when determining trips.
  • Signed consent forms must be collected at least three school days before the scheduled trip and submitted to the respective Assistant Principal.
  • A trip description family letter must be sent home to parents prior to the day of the field trip.
  • Meal request forms must be submitted to the Food Service Supervisor no less than 2 weeks prior to the trip date.
  • All children must attend. If there is a concern about a particular child attending, the parent must be notified and given the opportunity to accompany the child — every child is expected to participate.
  • No trips may be scheduled on days of school-wide events, including concerts.
  • The last Friday of May is the deadline for field trips this school year.

Chancellor Regulations on Parent-Teacher Relationships

Conference Documentation & Follow-Up

Professional responsibilities around conference attendance, record-keeping, and ongoing communication.

Attendance is Required Required at all DOE scheduled conferences as part of your professional responsibility.
Keep a Conference Record Log each conference's student name, parent name, date, and time.
Rescheduling Missed Conferences Send a new appointment electronically with the day and time offered.
Keep Parents Informed Especially about lack of academic progress or behavior concerns (see guidelines below).

Parent Engagement Activities Menu

Approved activities that count toward your weekly parent engagement time (see Key Communication Info above).

  • Meetings (individual or group) with parents or guardians
  • Telephone conversations with parents or guardians
  • Written correspondence with parents or guardians
  • Creating newsletters
  • Creating content for school/class websites and answering machines
  • Preparing student report cards
  • Preparing student progress reports
  • Meetings with parents of English Language Learners
  • Preparing for Parent Engagement activities
  • Other mutually-agreed upon items

Building Healthy Family Relationships

General guidelines for building trust and partnership with families.

Lead with Warmth & Respect Families partner best when they feel valued, not judged.
Communicate Early & Often Share good news before there's a problem to report.
Be Clear & Consistent Use plain language and keep follow-through consistent.
Listen First Families are experts on their own children — ask and listen fully.
Meet Families Where They Are Offer multiple ways to connect, not just one default.
Stay Solution-Focused Pair concerns with a plan to problem-solve together.

NYS Next Gen & P.S. 175 Pedagogy

Instructional Math Shifts

The Next Generation Mathematics Learning Standards require three core shifts in instruction alongside student-centered problem-solving discourse.

1 Focus

Deepen focus on key grade-level priorities so students establish strong conceptual mastery before moving forward.

2 Coherence

Connect learning across grades to build on previous knowledge and establish seamless math progressions.

3 Rigor

Balance Conceptual Understanding, Procedural Skill & Fluency, and Real-World Application equally.

Try-Discuss-Connect Discourse Framework

Transition from traditional "I Do, We Do, You Do" instruction to student-centered inquiry: "Try" (individual or partner problem solving) → "Discuss" (sharing strategies and mathematical discourse) → "Connect" (synthesizing methods and formalizing mathematical concepts).
